title: Pruneboard: narrow-surface dashboard + tracing cut plan for Q2 console ship
creator: Lina Park
description:
Summary: We need to reduce the surface of the Redwood Console insight features (dashboards, tracing, cost breakdown) to meet the Q2 launch date while preserving critical developer workflows: 1) quick operational triage, 2) cost signal to detect spikes, and 3) the ability to see traceable slow requests. This ticket documents the explicit cuts, rationale, rollout and rollback guardrails, and acceptance criteria.

Context: The current PRD aimed to ship a broad set of tiles (per-route latency cards, per-tenant cost breakdowns, full trace flamegraphs, token-level cost timelines). Engineering capacity and telemetry budget require trimming. PM/Design/Eng alignment meeting 2025-02-26 prioritized developer enablement and fast failure mode (what helps an engineer find and fix production issues quickly).

Key goals for the trimmed surface:
- Maintain a compact Ops overview card (latency p50/p95, error rate, QPS) for routes.
- Keep a single cost heatline for the org (daily cost trend + 7d delta) but defer per-route cost slice.
- Provide sampled traces linking from the latency card to a lightweight trace inspector (span list + timing) rather than full flamegraphs or waterfall zoom.
- Ensure the Console still emits the minimal telemetry events for alerting/QA (route-level alerts, cost spike events).

Explicit MVP cuts (what we will NOT ship in Q2):
- Per-route granular cost breakdown tile (deferred to console-2025.06).
- Full flamegraph UI and timeline waterfall view for traces (deferred until tracing-1.1).
- Token-level cost timeline and per-token attribution in the UI (will remain in backend logs only).
- Historical retention beyond 30 days for telemetry visualizations (extended-retention will be an add-on).

Trade-offs & rationale:
- Removing per-route cost in the UI reduces immediate operational visibility for cost engineering teams, but preserves a global spike detector so on-call can be alerted and drill into logs. This minimizes frontend complexity and reduces required backend aggregation work.
- Replacing flamegraphs with a span-list reduces UI engineering and client-side render cost; engineers lose deep visual profiling but keep the ability to identify slow spans and offending services.
- Shortening telemetry retention reduces storage and infra costs required to meet the launch date; long-term analytics customers will be given migration guidance to queries + exports.

Rollout strategy and safety:
- Feature flag: pruneboard.mvp to gate trimmed surface. Default enabled for all orgs in staging.
- Canary: enable for 5% of production orgs for 72 hours, monitor error budget and frontend render latency.
- Telemetry gating: if frontend error rate > 0.5% or avg render time > 1.5s for the dashboard route, auto-roll back the flag.
- Manual rollback playbook documented in Confluence (link below) and on-call notified via Slack runbook channel.

Links to artifacts and references:
- PRD (trimmed-surface): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Pruneboard+MVP+Trimmed+PRD
- Design mocks (keeps-only): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/pruneboard-mvp
- Engineering breakdown/ticket epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/labels/pruneboard-mvp
- Telemetry dashboard (canary health): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ops/pruneboard-canary
- Rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Console+Rollback+Runbook
decisions: Cut per-route cost tile: defers backend aggregation and frontend cost-slicing work to 2025.06
Remove flamegraphs: keep lightweight span list + link to raw trace export
Keep global cost heatline and daily delta: preserves alerting signal for cost spikes
Limit retention to 30 days for visualizations in MVP: reduces infra/time-to-ship risk
acceptance_criteria: A1: Dashboard ops card renders in under 1s on 95th percentile in staging with sample orgs
A2: Global cost heatline shows daily totals + 7d delta and matches billing data within 3% for last 7 days
A3: Clicking from latency card opens a sampled trace inspector with span list and timestamps within 500ms
A4: Feature flag pruneboard.mvp can be toggled via Console and honors rollout percentages
A5: Canary telemetry shows frontend error rate < 0.5% and avg render time < 1.5s over 72h in canary cohort
A6: Documentation: Rollback runbook, design rationale, and scope-decision log published in Confluence
comments: 2025-03-01 - Nora Chen: Alignment call notes: Eng asked to defer per-route cost because aggregation work spills into backend API changes; agreed to keep cost heatline and provide a CSV export as a temporary workaround.
2025-03-02 - Mateo Ruiz (Eng): Engineering estimate updated: frontend work 3pts, backend telemetry plumbing 5pts. Will need a small infra spike to ensure sample traces are retained for 24h.
2025-03-04 - Priya Shah (Design): Design sign-off on span-list inspector. Added accessibility checks and reduced visual density for initial ship.
2025-03-05 - Lina Park: Final decision logged — proceed with trimmed surface. Nora to coordinate canary schedule with Eng and SRE.
